cards.title: Torah Citation: 'The Life for the Life, and the Eye for the Eye'
cards.note: Surah 5:45 explicitly cites the Torah's law of retaliation ('The life for the life, and the eye for the eye, and the nose for the nose, and the ear for the ear, and the tooth for the tooth'), matching Exodus 21:22–25 and Leviticus 24:19–20.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr note that Surah 5:45 explicitly quotes the legal ruling God revealed to Moses in the Torah.
discussion.reply: Surah 5:45 reproduces the sequence of clauses found in the extant books of Exodus 21:23–25 and Leviticus 24:19–20 ('life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth') and calls upon the Jews of Medina to judge by the written Torah in their possession.

cards.quranEn: We prescribed for them in it: ‘The life for the life, and the eye for the eye, and the nose for the nose, and the ear for the ear, and the tooth for the tooth, and (for) the wounds retaliation.’ But whoever remits it as a freewill offering, it will be an atonement for him. Whoever does not judge by what God has sent down, those – they are the evildoers.
quranHighlights: ‘The life for the life, and the eye for the eye, and the nose for the nose, and the ear for the ear, and the tooth for the tooth, and (for) the wounds retaliation.’

sources.en: And whoever shall inflict a blemish on his neighbor, as he has done to him, so shall it be done to himself in return; bruise for bruise, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: as any one may inflict a blemish on a man, so shall it be rendered to him.

cards.title: Psalms Citation: 'The Earth — My Righteous Servants Will Inherit It'
cards.note: Surah 21:105 explicitly cites the Psalms (al-Zabūr) by name ('We have written in the Psalms, after the Reminder: The earth – My righteous servants will inherit it'), quoting Psalm 37:29 (LXX 36:29) and its restatement in Matthew 5:5.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes state that God here quotes the verbatim promise previously revealed to David in the Psalms (al-Zabūr) after the Torah.
discussion.reply: The clause 'The earth – My righteous servants will inherit it' matches the exact wording of Psalm 37:29 (LXX 36:29, 'the righteous shall inherit the earth') preserved in Hebrew and Greek manuscripts predating Islam by centuries.

cards.quranEn: Certainly We have written in the Psalms, after the Reminder: ‘The earth – My righteous servants will inherit it.’

cards.title: Excluding the Arrogant 'Until the Camel Passes Through the Eye of the Needle'
cards.note: Surah 7:40 declares that those who reject God's signs will not enter the Garden 'until the camel passes through the eye of the needle,' reproducing Jesus' proverb in Matthew 19:24 and Luke 18:25 alongside its Talmudic counterpart in Berakhot 55b.

discussion.view: Classical commentators explain this clause as a vivid Arabic proverb illustrating an impossibility, or as a shared truth spoken by earlier prophets.
discussion.reply: In the Synoptic Gospels (Matthew 19:24; Luke 18:25), Jesus coins the image of a camel passing through the eye of a needle regarding entry into the kingdom of God, while the Babylonian Talmud (Berakhot 55b) adapts it to an elephant; Surah 7:40 places the Gospel wording directly into divine speech.

cards.quranEn: Surely those who call Our signs a lie, and are arrogant about it – the gates of the sky will not be opened for them, nor will they enter the Garden, until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. In this way We repay the sinners.
quranHighlights: nor will they enter the Garden, until the camel passes through the eye of the needle.

cards.title: Gospel Citation: 'Like a Seed That Puts Forth Its Shoot and Stands Straight'
cards.note: Surah 48:29 cites 'their image in the Gospel' as 'a seed that puts forth its shoot, and strengthens it, and it becomes stout and stands straight on its stalk, pleasing the sowers,' reproducing the Parable of the Growing Seed in Mark 4:26–29.

discussion.view: Classical tafsīr traditions hold that Surah 48:29 quotes a prophetic description of Muḥammad's companions written in the original Injīl.
discussion.reply: The sequence of botanical stages in Surah 48:29 ('puts forth its shoot, and strengthens it, and it becomes stout and stands straight on its stalk') reproduces Jesus' Parable of the Growing Seed in Mark 4:26–29 ('the seed sprouts and grows... first the blade, then the head, then the mature grain in the head'), where the parable describes the kingdom of God.

cards.quranEn: Muḥammad is the messenger of God. Those who are with him are harsh against the disbelievers, (but) compassionate among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating themselves, seeking favor from God and approval. Their marks on their faces are the trace of prostration. That is their image in the Torah, and their image in the Gospel is like a seed (that) puts forth its shoot, and strengthens it, and it becomes stout and stands straight on its stalk, pleasing the sowers – so that He may enrage the disbelievers by means of them. God has promised those of them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward.
quranHighlights: their image in the Gospel is like a seed (that) puts forth its shoot, and strengthens it, and it becomes stout and stands straight on its stalk, pleasing the sowers

sources.title: New Testament (NASB) - Gospel of Mark
sources.en: And He was saying, "The kingdom of God is like a man who casts seed upon the soil; and he goes to bed at night and gets up by day, and the seed sprouts and grows-- how, he himself does not know. "The soil produces crops by itself; first the blade, then the head, then the mature grain in the head. "But when the crop permits, he immediately puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come."

first the blade, then the head, then the mature grain in the head.

cards.title: Calling Across the Partition: 'Pour Some Water on Us' From the Garden
cards.note: In Surah 7:44–50, the companions of the Fire call across a partition (ḥijāb) to the companions of the Garden, 'Pour some water on us,' and are told it is forbidden, mirroring the Rich Man begging Abraham across the chasm for water in Luke 16:22–26.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators view this dialogue across the partition as a prophetic depiction of the Hereafter confirming truths taught by earlier messengers.
discussion.reply: The structural elements in Surah 7:44–50—the damned recognizing the blessed across an impassable barrier, crying out for water to cool their torment in the flame, and receiving a refusal—follow the narrative sequence of Jesus' parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus in Luke 16:22–26.

cards.quranEn: [44] The companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire: ‘We have found what our Lord promised us (to be) true. So have you found what your Lord promised (to be) true?’ They will say, ‘Yes!’ And then a caller will call out among them: ‘The curse of God is on the evildoers, [45] who keep (people) from the way of God and desire (to make) it crooked, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.’ [46] Between both (groups) of them (there is) a partition, and on the heights (there are) men who recognize each (of them) by their marks, and they call out to the companions of the Garden: ‘Peace (be) upon you! They have not entered it, as much as they were eager (to do so).’ [47] And when their sight is turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, ‘Our Lord, do not place us among the people who are evildoers.’ [48] The men of the heights will call out to men whom they recognize by their marks, (and) say, ‘Your hoarding is of no use to you, nor what you were arrogant (about). [49] Are these the ones whom you swore God would not reach with (His) mercy? Enter the Garden! (There will be) no fear on you, nor will you sorrow.’ [50] And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of the Garden: ‘Pour some water on us, or some of what God has provided you!’ They will say, ‘Surely God has forbidden both to the disbelievers,

cards.title: 'Wait for Us, Let Us Take From Your Light' Outside the Shut Door
cards.note: In Surah 57:13–14, hypocrites say to believers 'Wait for us, let us take from your light,' are told to turn back and search for light, and are shut outside a gated wall, matching the Foolish Virgins in Matthew 25:7–12.

discussion.view: Classical exegetes explain this scene as an eschatological event on the bridge (al-ṣirāṭ) where hypocrites lose their light and are separated from believers by a gated wall.
discussion.reply: Surah 57:13–14 reproduces the three sequential beats of Jesus' Parable of the Ten Virgins in Matthew 25:7–12: the plea to share light ('Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out'), the dismissal to go obtain it elsewhere ('go instead to the dealers and buy some for yourselves'), and the shutting of the door between the two groups.

cards.quranEn: [13] On the Day when the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say to those who believed: ‘Wait for us! Let us borrow your light!’ It will be said, ‘Turn back and search for a light!’ And a wall with a door will be set up between them: on the inside of it (there is) mercy, and on the outside of it – facing (it) – (there is) the punishment. [14] They will call out to them: ‘Were we not with you?’ They will say, ‘Yes, indeed! But you tempted yourselves, and you waited and doubted, and wishful thinking deceived you, until the command of God came, and the Deceiver deceived you about God.
quranHighlights: ‘Wait for us! Let us borrow your light!’ It will be said, ‘Turn back and search for a light!’ And a wall with a door will be set up between them

"And while they were going away to make the purchase, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast; and the door was shut. "Later the other virgins also came, saying, 'Lord, lord, open up for us.' "But he answered, 'Truly I say to you, I do not know you.

cards.title: Promise in the Garden: 'Neither to Hunger Nor Thirst Nor Be Struck by the Sun'
cards.note: Surah 20:118–119 promises Adam in the Garden 'not to hunger there or go naked, nor to thirst there' or feel the sun's heat, matching the exact clause sequence of Isaiah 49:10 and Revelation 7:16 ('They will hunger no longer, nor thirst anymore').

discussion.view: Muslim commentators interpret these four paired clauses as God's direct assurance to Adam that the Garden provides complete shelter and sustenance.
discussion.reply: The Genesis Eden narrative contains no such fourfold formula; instead, the paired promise ('not hunger... nor thirst... nor shall the sun strike them') is a distinctive prophetic and apocalyptic formula from Isaiah 49:10 and Revelation 7:16 that Surah 20:118–119 retrojects into the address to Adam.

cards.quranEn: [118] Surely it is yours not to hunger there or go naked, [119] nor to thirst there or be exposed to the sun.’

nor to thirst there or be exposed to the sun.’

cards.title: 'We Shall Roll Up the Sky Like the Rolling Up of a Scroll for the Writings'
cards.note: Surah 21:104 depicts Judgment Day as 'the Day when We shall roll up the sky like the rolling up of a scroll for the writings,' reproducing the cosmic scroll simile of Isaiah 34:4 ('the sky shall be rolled up like a scroll') and Revelation 6:14.

discussion.view: Classical commentators explain this verse as a shared prophetic depiction of the end of the cosmos revealed across scriptural dispensations.
discussion.reply: The specific simile comparing the collapsing firmament to a scribe rolling up a written scroll originates in Isaiah 34:4 and is repeated in Revelation 6:14 ('The sky was split apart like a scroll when it is rolled up'), demonstrating direct continuity with biblical apocalyptic phraseology.

cards.quranEn: On the Day when We shall roll up the sky like the rolling up of a scroll for the writings: as We brought about the first creation, (so) We shall restore it – (it is) a promise (binding) on Us. Surely We shall do (it)!
quranHighlights: On the Day when We shall roll up the sky like the rolling up of a scroll for the writings

cards.title: Answering Scoffers: 'A Day With Your Lord Is Like a Thousand Years'
cards.note: When challengers demand that punishment be hurried, Surah 22:47 replies that 'God will not break His promise; surely a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count,' matching 2 Peter 3:8–9 and Psalm 90:4 (LXX 89:4).

discussion.view: Exegetes note that this verse answers Meccan sceptics who mocked the delay of divine judgment by contrasting human time with God's eternal measure.
discussion.reply: While Psalm 90:4 (LXX 89:4) introduces the comparison of a thousand years to a day passed, 2 Peter 3:8–9 specifically deploys the maxim ('with the Lord one day is like a thousand years. The Lord is not slow about His promise') to answer scoffers questioning the delay of judgment—the exact rhetorical context and sequence reproduced in Surah 22:47.

cards.quranEn: They seek to hurry you with the punishment. God will not break His promise. Surely a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.
quranHighlights: God will not break His promise. Surely a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.

cards.title: Creating the World in Six Days and 'No Weariness Touched Us'
cards.note: Surah 50:38 states that God created the heavens and earth in six days and adds 'No weariness touched Us in doing that,' matching Bereishit Rabbah 10:9 ('It was not with toil and not with exertion that the Holy One created His world') and Isaiah 40:28.

discussion.view: al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr report that Surah 50:38 was revealed to refute a Jewish claim that God rested on the seventh day to recover from fatigue.
discussion.reply: While Genesis 2:2 and Exodus 31:17 state that God 'ceased and rested' on the seventh day, neither the Hebrew Bible nor rabbinic tradition teaches that God experienced fatigue: Isaiah 40:28 explicitly states that the Creator 'shall not hunger, nor be weary,' and Bereishit Rabbah 10:9 explains Genesis 2:2 in the exact terms echoed by Surah 50:38 ('It was not with toil and not with exertion that the Holy One blessed be He created His world').

cards.quranEn: Certainly We created the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, in six days. No weariness touched Us in (doing) that.
quranHighlights: We created the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, in six days. No weariness touched Us in (doing) that.

cards.title: 'Do Not Say of Anything: I Will Do That Tomorrow, Except: If God Pleases'
cards.note: Surah 18:23–24 commands 'Do not say of anything, Surely I am going to do that tomorrow, except: If God pleases,' matching James 4:13–15 ('Today or tomorrow we will go... Instead, you ought to say, If the Lord wills, we will live and also do this').

discussion.view: Commentators record that these verses admonished the Prophet after he promised to answer three questions from Meccan challengers 'tomorrow' without adding 'If God wills.'
discussion.reply: The two-part rhetorical structure—forbidding the statement 'I will do that tomorrow' and prescribing the exact conditional formula 'If the Lord wills, we will... do this or that'—matches the Greek New Testament Epistle of James (4:13–15), written in the first century AD.

cards.quranEn: [23] And do not say of anything, ‘Surely I am going to do that tomorrow,’ [24] except (with the proviso): ‘If God pleases.’ And remember your Lord, when you forget, and say, ‘It may be that my Lord will guide me to something nearer the right (way) than this.’

cards.title: 'Do Not Lay on Us a Burden Such as You Laid on Those Before Us'
cards.note: Surah 2:286 states 'God does not burden any person beyond his capacity' and prays 'do not lay on us a burden such as You laid on those before us,' matching Acts 15:10 ('a yoke which neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear') and 1 Cor 10:13.

discussion.view: Muslim tradition regards the closing verses of Surah al-Baqarah as a direct heavenly gift relieving the Muslim community of the strict legal covenants imposed on earlier nations.
discussion.reply: The two central clauses of Surah 2:286—that God does not test a person 'beyond what you are able' and the appeal against bearing a legal 'yoke which neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear'—parallel Paul's wording in 1 Corinthians 10:13 and Peter's speech at the Jerusalem Council in Acts 15:10.

cards.quranEn: God does not burden any person beyond his capacity. What they have earned is either to their credit or against their account. ‘Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, do not lay on us a burden such as You laid on those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us beyond what we have the strength (to bear). Pardon us, and forgive us, and have compassion on us. You are our Protector. Help us against the people who are disbelievers.’
quranHighlights: God does not burden any person beyond his capacity.

cards.title: Jews and Christians Saying: 'We Are the Sons of God, and His Beloved'
cards.note: Surah 5:18 quotes Jews and Christians saying 'We are the sons of God, and His beloved,' matching Rabbi Akiva's saying in Pirkei Avot 3:14 ('Beloved are Israel in that they were called children to the All-Present') and 1 John 3:1.

discussion.view: Commentators explain that Surah 5:18 records and rejects the verbal boast of seventh-century Jewish and Christian communities claiming special filial standing before God.
discussion.reply: While Deuteronomy 14:1 and 1 John 3:1 call believers 'children of God,' the specific pairing of the two predicates ('sons of God, and His beloved') reproduces Rabbi Akiva's famous saying in Mishnah Pirkei Avot 3:14 ('Beloved are Israel in that they were called children to the All-Present') and treats a metaphor of covenantal love as a literal claim to exemption from divine chastisement.

cards.quranEn: The Jews and the Christians say, ‘We are the sons of God, and His beloved.’ Say: ‘Then why does He punish you for your sins? No! You are human beings, (part) of what He created. He forgives whomever He pleases and He punishes whomever He pleases. To God (belongs) the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them. To Him is the (final) destination.’
quranHighlights: The Jews and the Christians say, ‘We are the sons of God, and His beloved.’

cards.title: Sinai Covenant Inversion: 'We Hear and Disobey' vs. 'We Will Hear, and Do'
cards.note: Surah 2:93 reports the Israelites answering at Sinai 'We hear and disobey,' inverting the biblical Sinai covenant pledge 'We will hear, and do' in Deuteronomy 5:27 and its celebration in Talmud Bavli Shabbat 88a.

discussion.view: Classical commentators explain that while the Israelites spoke obedience with their tongues at Sinai, their rebellious hearts inwardly replied 'We hear and disobey.'
discussion.reply: In Deuteronomy 5:27, Israel pledges at Sinai 'we will hear, and do' (Hebrew shamaʿnu we-ʿasinu), a phrase celebrated in Talmud Bavli Shabbat 88a; because the Hebrew verb ʿasinu ('we will do') sounds like the Arabic verb ʿaṣaynā ('we disobey'), Surah 2:93 turns the Torah's vow of obedience into a declaration of defiance ('We hear and disobey').

cards.quranEn: And when We took a covenant with you, and raised the mountain above you: ‘Hold fast what We have given you, and hear,’ they said, ‘We hear and disobey.’ And they were made to drink the calf in their hearts because of their disbelief. Say: ‘Evil is what your belief commands you, if you are believers.’
quranHighlights: And when We took a covenant with you, and raised the mountain above you: ‘Hold fast what We have given you, and hear,’ they said, ‘We hear and disobey.’

cards.title: 'In a Day, the Measure of Which Is a Thousand Years of What You Count'
cards.note: Surah 32:5 declares that the cosmic affair ascends to God 'in a day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count,' matching Psalm 90:4 (LXX 89:4), 2 Peter 3:8 ('with the Lord one day is like a thousand years'), and Jubilees 4:30.

discussion.view: Commentators interpret the thousand-year day of Surah 32:5 either as the span of cosmic administration or as the length of a day in the Hereafter.
discussion.reply: The formula equating one divine day with a thousand human years is an established Second Temple and New Testament exegetical tradition rooted in Psalm 90:4 (LXX 89:4) and formulated explicitly in Jubilees 4:30 ('one thousand years are as one day in the testimony of the heavens') and 2 Peter 3:8.

cards.quranEn: He directs the (whole) affair from the sky to the earth; then it will go up to Him in a day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count.
quranHighlights: in a day, the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count.
